item.title: Hike Review: Piethorne Reservoir
item.description:
🥾 Piethorn Reservoir Winter Hike Review

Piethorne is one of those walks that never quite feels the same twice, and this late December outing was very much a case of embracing the conditions rather than fighting them.

We headed out for a brisk morning hike, mainly to get the blood flowing and clear the head before the rest of the day. From the off, the weather set the tone foggy, misty and damp, with a light drizzle hanging in the air. Not unpleasant, but definitely the sort of weather that seeps into your clothes if you’re not paying attention.

item.title: Film Review: The Running Man (2025)
item.description:
🎬 The Running Man (2025) Review

The Running Man (2025), directed by Edgar Wright and starring Glen Powell, is a high-energy, visually striking remake of the earlier action classic. While I’m not sure it compares completely with the original maybe that’s just sentimentality talking the special effects and cinematography are certainly an upgrade in this version, and it made for an enjoyable watch all the same.

item.description:

The film focuses on the true story of the psychological duel between US Army psychiatrist Douglas Kelley (Rami Malek) and the imprisoned Nazi leader Hermann Göring (Russell Crowe) during the first Nuremberg trial in 1945-1946. item.title: Ingleton Falls Hike
item.description:
Ingleton Falls Hike (Fierce Storm Waterfalls)

We tackled the always-awesome Ingleton Waterfalls Trail just a day after Storm Claudia, and it completely transformed the experience.

item.description:
🏔️ Hiking to the Top of Whernside

Whernside is the tallest of the Yorkshire Three Peaks, and although it’s often called the gentler giant, the weather on this trip decided otherwise, still in the midst of a storm so we got lucky. We began at the mighty Ribblehead Viaduct, an iconic and dramatic starting point.

Only a short way into the route, we reached a stunning waterfall section a perfect early highlight before the long, steady ridge climb.

item.title: Review: Fawlty Towers The Play Palace Theatre Manchester
item.description:
Review

I managed to snag a couple of cheap tickets via Tickets and landed in the Palace Theatre for the touring production of Fawlty Towers The Play. The evening is an affectionate, often uproarious stage distillation of John Cleese’s original sitcom. Cast & performances

item.title: Skiddaw Summit via Jenkins Bridleway
item.description:
Hiking to Skiddaw Summit & Little Man

Overview

Parking isnt great and you need to arrive early to have any chance of a parking space (the car park is small). Otherwise this was a fantastic hike with great views. We even managed to experience a cloud inversion.

After some early clag this cleared and its a pretty steep and brutal ascent. We took in Skiddaw little man also and recommend you tackle this afer summitting.

Key Hike Points

  • Steep but rewarding ascent

item.description:
🚂 A Day in Brontë Country

Keighley and Haworth have long sat high on my list of places to visit properly not just as a whistle stop tourist stop, but as somewhere to walk, linger and absorb.
